newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat, looking at balances.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat, looking at balances.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds steadied from unchanged to an eighth of a point higher in late trade on Wednesday even though dealers were stuck with balances on some new issues.
"I think there is a fair amount of going-away business, I just think they priced some of the new issues pretty aggressively, a little ahead of the market," a trader said.

The list of issuers stuck with balances included the State of Ohio Highway Capital Improvements, which had a $36 million balance out of $125 million, Texas A&M University, which had a $22 million balance out of its nearly $65 million sale, and Washington Suburban Sanitary District, which had a $28.5 million balance left out of its over $71 million sale.
Still, at least some issuers were able to sell their bonds at slightly higher prices than they first anticipated.

The week, which has seen underwriting volumes rise, included the sale of $566 million bonds by Puerto Rico Building Authority, which Smith Barney repriced, lowering yields in several maturities and cutting the top yield in 2027 by one basis point to 5.50 percent.
And New York State Dormitory Authority repriced $67 million of bonds by reducing yields in several maturities.

The ratio of triple-A, 30-year municipal bonds yielded 79.2 percent of 30-year U.S. Treasuries, only up two-tenths of a percentage point from Tuesday's reading which was the lowest level in more than two years, according to Delphis Hanover Corp.
Tuesday's ratio was the lowest since March 7, 1995, when munis were yielding 78.6 percent of long Treasuries, a Delphis analyst said.

On Thursday, negotiated issues expected to come to market totaled over $407 million in 13 sales, with more than $218 million of competitive deals anticipated in 15 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Thursday's schedule of negotiated offerings included a $188 million sale of revenue bonds by Tyler Health Facilities in Texas, while an over $75 million sale of Rhode Island general obligations and a nearly $55 million sale by the New Jersey EDA led the competitive list.
North Arizona University's offering of almost $31 million of revenue bonds was expected to draw interest in part because so little debt is sold by issuers in that state.
In the secondary market, Denver, Colorado City and County Airport Revenues of 2025, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.66 percent, NET, down two basis points.
And Dallas-Fort Worth, Texas, Regulatory Airport Revenues of 2023, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.73 percent, NET, unchanged.

September U.S. Treasury bonds rose two ticks to 110-19/32, while September municipal bond futures rose eight ticks to 116-20/32. This left the MOB spread between the two futures contracts, both of which trade on the Chicago Board of Trade, at plus 193 ticks, slightly firmer.
